question_en: Which of the following is typically equal to zero at the initiation of an interest rate swap contract?
option_c: Neither its value nor its price.
explanation_en: As with other derivatives, the price of an interest rate swap (the fixed rate specified in the contract) is typically set such that the value of the swap is zero at initiation.

subtopic: Reading 74 Pricing and Valuation of Interest Rates and Other Swaps
question_en: An investor could best replicate the position of the floating rate payer in a swap by:
option_a: borrowing at a oating rate and entering a series of zero-value FRAs.
option_b: borrowing at a oating rate and buying a xed-rate bond.
option_c: borrowing at a xed rate and entering a series of zero-value FRAs.
explanation_en: The investor in the swap will pay the reference rate and receive fixed-rate payments (on a notional principal amount). The net payments can be replicated by borrowing at a floating rate and investing the proceeds in a fixed-rate bond. The payments could also be replicated by taking a floating-rate loan (or issuing a floating-rate bond) and entering a series of FRAs, but these would not necessarily (or likely) be zero-value FRAs; zero-value FRAs would typically not all have the same fixed rate as swap payments do.

subtopic: Reading 74 Pricing and Valuation of Interest Rates and Other Swaps
question_en: The price of a fixed-for-floating interest rate swap contract:
option_a: may vary over the life of the contract.
option_c: is directly related to changes in the oating rate.
explanation_en: The price of a swap contract is set such that the contract has a value of zero at initiation. The value of a fixed-for-floating interest rate swap contract may vary over its life as the floating rate changes.

subtopic: Reading 74 Pricing and Valuation of Interest Rates and Other Swaps
question_en: For a series of forward contracts to replicate a swap contract, the forward contracts must have:
option_a: values at swap initiation that sum to zero.
option_b: values at swap expiration that sum to zero.
option_c: values at swap initiation that are equal to zero.
explanation_en: When replicating a swap with a series of forward contracts, each forward contract is likely to have a non-zero value at initiation, but they can replicate a swap with a value of zero at initiation if the values of the forward contracts sum to zero at swap initiation.

subtopic: Reading 75 Pricing and Valuation of Options
question_en: Which of the following statements about the difference in arbitrage in pricing forward commitments and options is correct?
option_a: Both the forward buyer and the option buyer pay no cash upfront.
option_b: The forward buyer has an unlimited loss but the option buyer has a limited loss at maturity when the underlying is a stock.
option_c: Only options have upper and lower no-arbitrage price bounds.
explanation_en: Because options are contingent claims, the right to exercise or not to exercise the option leads to establishing both upper and lower price bounds on options. In contrast, forward commitments represent obligations on both sides, and therefore there are no price bounds. However, there is a lower bound in cases where the underlying cannot have a negative value, for example, stocks. While the forward buyer pays no cash upfront, the option buyer pays a premium upfront.

question_en: Which of the following statements about moneyness is most accurate? When the stock price is:
option_a: below the strike price, a call option is in-the-money.
option_b: above the strike price, a put option is in-the-money.
option_c: above the strike price, a put option is out-of-the-money.
explanation_en: When the stock price is above the strike price, a put option is out-of-the-money. When the stock price is below the strike price, a call option is out-of-the-money.

subtopic: Reading 75 Pricing and Valuation of Options
question_en: The time value of an option is most accurately described as:
option_a: the amount by which the intrinsic value exceeds the option premium.
option_b: equal to the entire premium for an out-of-the-money option.
option_c: increasing as the option approaches its expiration date.
explanation_en: The price (or premium) of an option is its intrinsic value plus its time value. An out-of-the- money option has an intrinsic value of zero, so its entire premium consists of time value. Time value is zero at an option's expiration date. Time value is the amount by which an option's premium exceeds its intrinsic value.

explanation_en: A put option gives its owner the right to sell the underlying good at a specified exercise price for a specified time period. When the stock's price is less than the exercise price a put option has value and is said to be in-the-money.

question_en: An increase in the riskless rate of interest, other things equal, will:
option_a: decrease call option values and decrease put option values.
option_b: decrease call option values and increase put option values.
option_c: increase call option values and decrease put option values.
explanation_en: An increase in the risk-free rate of interest will increase call option values and decrease put option values.

subtopic: Reading 75 Pricing and Valuation of Options
question_en: The value of a put option at expiration is most likely to be increased by:
option_c: higher volatility of the underlying asset price.
explanation_en: The value of an option at expiration is the greater of zero or its exercise value. A higher exercise price increases the exercise value of a put option because it gives the holder the right to sell the underlying asset for a higher price. The risk-free interest rate and volatility of the underlying asset price only affect the time value of options, which is zero at expiration.

subtopic: Reading 75 Pricing and Valuation of Options
question_en: For a European style put option:
option_a: time value is equal to its market price minus its exercise value.
option_b: intrinsic value is equal to its market price plus its exercise value.
option_c: exercise value is equal to the underlying stock price minus its exercise price.
explanation_en: The time value of an option (either a put or a call) is equal to its market price minus its exercise value. A put's exercise value is the maximum of zero or its exercise price minus the stock price. Intrinsic value is another term for exercise value.

question_en: A call option that is in the money:
option_a: has an exercise price less than the market price of the asset.
option_b: has an exercise price greater than the market price of the asset.
option_c: has a value greater than its purchase price.
explanation_en: A call option is in the money when the exercise price is less than the market price of the asset.

subtopic: Reading 75 Pricing and Valuation of Options
question_en: An investor holds two options on the same underlying stock, a call option with an exercise price of 25 and a put option with an exercise price of 30. If the market price of the stock is 27:
option_a: only one of the options is in the money.
option_b: both options are in the money.
option_c: neither option is in the money.
explanation_en: Both options are in the money. The put option is in the money because the option holder has the right to sell the stock for more than its market price. The call option is in the money because the option holder has the right to buy the stock for less than its market price.

question_en: A one-year European call option has an exercise price of X = $500. At the time of the option's purchase, the underlying asset trades at S0 = $485, and the risk-free rate is r = 1.25%. What is the no-arbitrage upper bound of this option in six months, if the underlying asset price is St = $510?
explanation_en: The upper bound of this option is simply the underlying asset price because no call buyer would pay more for the option than the asset's market price.

question_en: An investor has bought a European put option and written a European call option. Other things equal, a decrease in the risk-free rate will increase the value of:
option_a: only one of these option positions.
explanation_en: A decrease in the risk-free rate would decrease call option values and increase put option values. Because this investor is short calls and long puts, both positions would increase in value.

question_en: The upper bound of a European put option is the:
option_b: difference between the present value of the exercise price and the underlying asset price.
option_c: present value of the exercise price.
explanation_en: Because European puts cannot be exercised prior to expiration, their maximum value (or upper bound) is the present value of the exercise price, discounted at the risk-free rate, or X / (1 + Rf)(T–t).
